request: Add a check in the accounts views that validates the post-login `next` URL is one of our own pages.

summary.result_text:
I added the check in `hc/accounts/views.py`, but I haven't run the tests. The test command needed approval and I didn't get it.

The login views already called `_allow_redirect()` in four places (after login, the 2FA redirect, the magic-link request and the profile view). That function didn't exist. The file only had `_allow_next_url()`, which accepted any path starting with a single `/`, and nothing called it. I replaced it with `_allow_redirect()`, so the existing calls now work.

`_allow_redirect()` accepts a `next` URL only if all of these hold:
- It is non-empty, starts with `/`, and has no backslash.
- It has no scheme or host, so `//evil.com`, `https://…` and `/\evil.com` are all rejected.
- Its path resolves to one of the routes in the existing `POST_LOGIN_ROUTES` list (checks, details, log, channels, the Slack, Pushover and Telegram add pages, project settings, uncloak). That is why the existing tests treat `?next=/evil/` as invalid.

To run the tests: `python manage.py test hc.accounts.tests.test_login hc.accounts.tests.test_check_token hc.accounts.tests.test_login_totp hc.accounts.tests.test_login_webauthn`

input.command: python manage.py test hc.accounts.tests.test_login hc.accounts.tests.test_check_token hc.accounts.tests.test_login_totp hc.accounts.tests.test_login_webauthn 2>&1 | tail -15
